messages:
support_alex: FYI -- Vividly hitting sustained 429s and big latency spikes on their dedicated pool `vividly-prod-pool` since 09:12 UTC. Observed pattern: short spikes to 3x baseline QPS, then autoscale lag + auth retries amplify the tail.
customer_ops_julia: Confirming. Baseline QPS ~120 rps, peak bursts ~380 rps for ~30-90s. 95p latency climbs from 120ms -> 2.1s. They reported 401s intermittently right before the 429s.
support_alex: We have network logs and api-gateway traces attached in the ticket. Quick snapshot: pool utilization jumped to 92% during peaks, queued requests increased, and autoscaler only added replicas after ~70s.
opsbot: ALERT: high_429_rate detected for pool=vividly-prod-pool (429s=18% over 5m) @ 2267890305
cheng: Can you paste the autoscale config for that pool? I want to check thresholds + cooldown.
support_alex: Here is the config they gave:
```
min_replicas: 2
max_replicas: 8
scale_up_threshold: 75
scale_down_threshold: 30
scale_step: 1
cooldown_seconds: 60
warmup_seconds: 120
```
cheng: Hmm. scale_up_threshold=75% and scale_step=1 means slow reaction to a 3x burst. warmup_seconds=120 also prevents the new replicas from serving warm KV/cache immediately. That fits noisy-neighbor/retry amplification.
sre_jen: Also saw auth-service returning 401 -> client retries with exponential backoff but still lots of concurrent retries. If auth flaps, upstream clients hit our pool more frequently while older connections are retrying. Could be billing/token rotation issue on Vividly side.
customer_ops_julia: We rotated their signing key yesterday at 08:50 UTC. They confirmed all tokens renewed but some older job workers may still use cached tokens for a few minutes.
runtime_tom: Short-term mitigations: increase min_replicas to 4 or 6 for their pool before peak windows, reduce cooldown_seconds to 20, increase scale_step to 2-3. Also enable pre-warm for new replicas: run lightweight noop load to populate KV cache.
cheng: Agreed. Also suggest adding request rate-based scaler (target_rps) instead of pure CPU/bucket util. For example set target_rps: 180 and max_scale_step: 3.
support_alex: Proposed immediate action (owner: runtime_tom):
- bump min_replicas to 4 for next 24h
- cooldown_seconds -> 20, scale_step -> 3
- enable prefilling/warmup on new nodes
- ask Vividly to pause token rotation during tomorrow's campaign window

Any objections?
sre_jen: +1. I'll also add an auth-health alert to our routing plane so we can short-circuit retries when upstream auth is failing (reduce amplification).
customer_ops_julia: I'll ask customer to confirm pause on rotation and identify any long-running worker processes. Also will share their internal retry config (we suspect aggressive retries).
cheng: Longer term: capacity plan notes for this tenant: target steady-state headroom 40% (so baseline 120 rps -> target capacity ~200 rps), set burst capacity to handle 400 rps for 2min windows with autoscale max 10 replicas. Add warmup hooks to autoscaler.
support_alex: I'll schedule a follow-up call with Vividly for 15:30 UTC and update the ticket. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
opsbot: ACTION_CREATED: runbook/vividly-capacity-adjust (owner=runtime_tom) @ 2267890589
